title: Selling on Amazon Saudi Arabia (KSA) and UAE: A Starter Guide
headline: Selling on Amazon Saudi Arabia (KSA) and the UAE: A Starter Guide
description: A starter guide to selling on Amazon.sa and Amazon.ae: why these marketplaces attract sellers, how registration works, fulfilment options, language and what to check before you launch.
link_label: Selling on Amazon KSA and UAE
body_html:
Amazon.ae (United Arab Emirates) and Amazon.sa (Saudi Arabia) are growing marketplaces where shoppers buy electronics, home and kitchen goods, beauty, fashion and more. Competition is often lower than on the largest marketplaces, which is one reason sellers look at them. This guide explains the starting points. Rules and fees change, so always confirm the details in Seller Central.

Why sellers look at KSA and UAE

  • A large, young, online-shopping population with strong mobile use.
  • Many categories still have fewer sellers than in the US or UK.
  • Both marketplaces can be managed from one regional selling account setup, so you can extend from one to the other.
  • Fast delivery matters to shoppers, and FBA helps you meet that expectation.

Registration in short

You register as a seller in the Middle East region. Expect to provide ID, company or trade details where required, a bank account, a card, and proof of address. Requirements for sellers outside the region can differ from those for local sellers, so read the current registration page before you start. Our account opening guide covers the general steps.

Fulfilment options

  • FBA: you send stock to Amazon's fulfilment centres in the region. Customers get fast delivery and the Prime-style badge. This is a good fit for steady sellers.
  • FBM: you ship to the customer yourself. It works for testing, bulky or custom items, but delivery speed and returns are on you. See our FBA vs FBM guide.

Language and listing content

Shoppers use both Arabic and English. A good English listing is a start, but adding Arabic titles and bullets can reach more buyers and improve conversion, especially in KSA. Make sure translations are natural, not literal.

Product and compliance checks

  • Check that your product category is open to you and not restricted or gated.
  • Check labelling, safety and import requirements for the product, for example for electronics, cosmetics and food.
  • Respect local culture and rules in your images and wording.
  • If you own a brand, register it in Brand Registry for control of your listings and access to A+ Content and sponsored ads.

Pricing and fees

Work out your landed cost: product, shipping to the region, customs and duties where they apply, Amazon's referral fee, fulfilment and storage fees. Prices are in local currency, so account for exchange-rate changes in your margin.

A simple launch plan

  • Choose a product with steady demand and a margin after all fees.
  • Build a strong listing with Arabic and English content.
  • Start with a small first shipment to test demand.
  • Run Sponsored Products ads to gain early sales. See our PPC basics guide.
  • Watch reviews and account health from the first week.
